source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Flink HA, Kubernetes/ZooKeeper HA, batch progress recovery, checkpointing, and metrics documentation; Apache Spark standalone and YARN deployment documentation; Apache Hadoop YARN ResourceManager restart and HA documentation; Kubernetes Lease documentation; etcd API documentation; and the primary Raft paper. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific HA and work-preservation claims are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed control state/event sequence, snapshots, coordinator identity/term, greatest accepted term, in-flight actions, worker/resource inventories, failover stage times, RPO/RTO, preserved/recomputed work, and unresolved actions.
Checked snapshot-plus-log replay, term comparison, end-to-end RTO, and work-preservation expressions with explicit domains and units.
Checked that election, discovery, lease, leadership belief, accepted fencing term, committed log position, checkpoint, external transaction, and terminal result remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Election and durable replay are necessary but insufficient without recipient-side fencing and external-action reconciliation.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced last sequence 5, committed task t1, reconciliation task t2, no runnable task, and successor term 8.
Checked the replay state transition sequence: t1 submit/assign/commit and t2 submit/commit-requested leave exactly one unresolved external action.
Checked snapshot example requires gap-free replay from 1001 through 1120 and exercise gap 5001 prevents proven recovery from a snapshot through 5000.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal lease duration, standby count, snapshot interval, replay limit, registration window, RPO, or RTO is prescribed.

evidence: Verified one effective leader from serialized increasing terms and greatest-term enforcement by every correctness-bearing recipient.
Verified deterministic state reconstruction from a complete snapshot at sequence j plus ordered integrity-checked events j+1 through k.
Verified stable-ID downstream lookup prevents unknown acknowledgement from becoming duplicate publication and terminal transitions cannot regress under stale evidence.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proofs explicitly depend on complete event history, deterministic transitions, durable downstream identities, and universal fencing coverage.

evidence: Reviewed crashes before/after append, acknowledgement, worker command, checkpoint completion, allocation request, commit, timer firing, snapshot publication, and terminal transition.
Reviewed process pause, lease expiry, simultaneous candidates, stale command, corrupt/truncated/gapped log, incompatible snapshot, reordered worker/resource reports, and dependency outage.
Reviewed partial/completed checkpoint, output timeout-after-commit, duplicate timer, reset retry budget, terminal worker report, mixed-version upgrade, rollback, and regional failover.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unproven history or external outcome remains unavailable/unknown or falls back to an explicit earlier recovery point; it is never synthesized.

evidence: Traced cluster/job identity, leader term, log sequence, snapshot/checksum/schema, graph/code/config, tasks/attempts/winners, resources, workers, checkpoints, transactions, timers, budgets, and terminal state.
Checked durable acknowledgement, snapshot/log alignment, stable IDs, fencing, bounded registration, worker/resource reconciliation, complete checkpoint selection, and timer reconstruction.
Checked HA-data retention, external dependency consistency, upgrade compatibility, one writer authority, and distinct failover versus disaster-recovery objectives.
invariant_checking.notes: Worker claims and live inventories are reconciliation evidence; durable coordinator and external-authority decisions remain authoritative.

evidence: Reviewed single-effective-leader, deterministic-replay, unknown-action-reconciliation, and terminal-monotonicity arguments with explicit assumptions.

Checked counterexamples for election without fencing, early acknowledgement, incomplete state persistence, unaligned snapshot/log, replayed API calls, early rescheduling, fresh timers/budgets, and local-only recovery.
Checked reference-state-machine comparison across crash, partition, response loss, corruption, report reordering, old-leader return, upgrade, and regional recovery histories.
proof_review.notes: Safety, control-state durability, work preservation, progress restoration, and regional data loss require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited coordinator, scheduler, driver, job manager, resource manager, leader, candidate, standby, term, lease, election, discovery, and fencing terminology.
Confirmed event log, commit index, control snapshot, checkpoint, worker inventory, resource inventory, external transaction, and status ledger are distinguished.
Confirmed process restart, active-passive failover, replicated state machine, work-preserving recovery, fallback restart, and regional disaster recovery are separate labels.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Flink, Spark, YARN, Kubernetes, etcd, and Raft concepts are not presented as identical implementations or guarantees.

evidence: Reviewed terms/transitions, renewal failures, fencing rejects, detection/election/discovery/load/replay/reconciliation/resume times, adopted work, unknown actions, and dependency failures.
Confirmed segmentation by job size/type, runtime/version, coordinator and storage domain, dependency, failure cause, recovery mode, and observation horizon.
Confirmed election latency, control availability, scheduling resume, restored useful throughput, work preservation, RPO, RTO, and blast radius are separately reported.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Fast leader election or many standbys is not mislabeled as complete recovery, zero data loss, or cross-domain availability.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed coordinator state, election/fencing, event logs, snapshots, failover order, worker/resource reconciliation, checkpoints/timers, unknown commits, work preservation, deployment/upgrade models, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable term-bearing RPCs, durable events, snapshot publication, staged failover, bounded registration, adoption/cancellation rules, allocation lookup, checkpoint selection, timer/budget recovery, transaction reconciliation, HA retention, upgrade canaries, and fault injection. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from control-state inventory through one-leader safety and replay to reconciliation, work preservation, and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover stale leaders, log replay, worker claims, allocations, checkpoints, timers, unknown commits, preserved shuffle, domains, and RTO evidence.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Flink/Spark/YARN/Kubernetes/etcd/Raft maintainer or author, coordinator/consensus/streaming/platform/SRE/security specialist, production control-plane operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
